answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making identity expensive to grow and cheap to verify: each agent must stake tokens and build a public history of useful work before its votes count. Like a trellis guiding vines, reputation channels growth along proven paths instead of letting fake identities spread across the meadow unchecked. A Sybil farm faces a cold tundra: every clone pays the same stake and time cost, so flooding the network costs more than any reward it could harvest.
